title: ADR-0050 — GitFlow Branching Strategy Rules
description: Machine-readable rules encoding ADR-0050 GitFlow Branching Strategy. Contractual branch naming, promotion policies, merge policies, and release tagging.

rules.title: Branch names follow pattern: type/ticket-id-description
rules.description: All branches MUST follow naming pattern: {type}/{ticket-id}-{short-description}. Types: feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/, release/, chore/.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Consistent naming enables automation and team coordination.

rules.title: Protected branches enforce direct push prohibition
rules.description: Direct push to protected branches (main, develop, qa, uat, release/*) is prohibited. All changes MUST come through pull requests with code review.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Protected branches require PR workflow for audit trail and review.
rules.validationQuery: GitHub/GitLab branch protection rules block direct push to main, develop, qa, uat, release/*.

rules.title: PR requires minimum 1 approved review
rules.description: Every pull request MUST have at least one approved code review before merge. Reviews must verify code quality, test coverage, and compliance with architectural standards.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Code review is mandatory for architectural compliance and knowledge sharing.
rules.validationQuery: PR merge blocked without minimum 1 approval. Reviewer cannot be the PR author.

rules.title: Release tags follow semver format
rules.description: Release tags MUST follow semantic versioning format: v{major}.{minor}.{patch} (e.g., v1.0.0, v2.3.1). Tags are created at release point from main branch.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Semver tags provide clear, auditable release history.

rules.title: Feature branches merge via squash or rebase
rules.description: Feature branches merge into develop using squash or rebase strategy to maintain clean history. Fast-forward merge when possible.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Squash/rebase keeps feature history clean while preserving commit granularity in PR.
rules.validationQuery: Feature → develop merges use squash or rebase. No merge commits on feature branches.

rules.title: Hotfixes follow expedited merge path
rules.description: Hotfixes branch from main (tagged release), apply fix, merge back to main AND develop simultaneously. Hotfixes skip code freeze restrictions but still require review.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Hotfixes need expedited path but cannot bypass review entirely.
rules.validationQuery: Hotfix branch merges to both main and develop. Both merges include same fix commit.

rules.title: Stale branches must be deleted after merge
rules.description: Branches MUST be deleted after successful merge. Feature/bugfix branches older than 30 days without activity are flagged as stale and subject to archive or removal.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Branch proliferation creates confusion about current state of development.
rules.validationQuery: Merged branches auto-deleted. Stale branch detection runs weekly.

rules.title: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
rules.description: Commit messages MUST follow Conventional Commits format: type(scope): description. Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Decision: Conventional Commits enables automated changelog generation and semantic release.
rules.validationQuery: Commit messages validated via commitlint or equivalent. Non-conforming commits blocked in CI.

rules.title: Environment promotion follows develop to qa to uat to main
rules.description: Promotions MUST follow the sequence develop -> qa -> uat -> main, with release/* inserted between uat and main when release hardening needs isolation.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Promotion Criteria: Environment branches represent deployable states and require evidence-based promotion.
rules.validationQuery: Promotion PR source and target follow develop->qa, qa->uat, uat->release/* or uat->main, release/*->main.

rules.title: Higher environments require stronger approval
rules.description: Pull requests into qa, uat, main, release/*, and hotfix/* MUST require at least two approvals unless an explicit incident exception applies.
rules.rationale: ADR-0050 §Pull Requests, Reviews, and Merge: Promotion branches need stronger review because they represent deployable environment states.
rules.validationQuery: Branch protection or repository rules require minimum two approvals for qa, uat, main, release/*, and hotfix/*.

exitCriteria.description: Branch naming validated in CI. Protected branches enforce PR workflow and promotion sequence. Release tags follow semver.
